events.response:
Designing a distributed consensus algorithm that can tolerate up to 1/3 of Byzantine nodes is a classic problem in fault-tolerant computing. The algorithm we will design is a modified version of the Practical Byzantine Fault Tolerance (PBFT) algorithm. This algorithm is known for its practicality and efficiency in achieving consensus in the presence of a large fraction of faulty nodes.
Algorithm: PBFT with Modified View Change Protocol
1. Node Initialization:
   - Each node n starts with an empty view V0 and an empty log L.
2. Request Processing:
   - When a node n receives a client request, it generates a Request object r containing the request and a unique identifier T.
   - n sends r to all other nodes in the network.
3. Pre-Prepare Phase:
   - Upon receiving r from node n, each node V prepares a Pre-Prepare message p containing r, T, and its own unique identifier N.
   - Node V sends p to all other nodes.
4. Prepare Phase:
   - When a node V receives a majority of Pre-Prepare messages p from other nodes, it prepares a Prepare message m containing p, T, N, and its local log L.
   - V sends m to all other nodes.
5. Commit Phase:
   - Upon receiving a majority of Prepare messages m from other nodes, V commits to the transaction contained in m by appending it to its log L.
   - V sends a Commit message c to all other nodes.
6. Client Response:
   - Upon receiving a Commit message c from a majority of nodes, n responds to the client with the result of the transaction.
7. View Change Protocol:
   - If a node detects a fault in the current view, it initiates a view change.
   - During a view change, each node transitions to a new view V' and resets its log.
   - The nodes then go through the Pre-Prepare, Prepare, and Commit phases with the new view.
Safety Property Proof:
To prove the safety property of this modified PBFT algorithm, we need to show that if a majority of nodes are honest, then the protocol will eventually reach a consensus on a value.
1. Validity: If a value v is committed in a view V, then v was proposed in a previous view V' and was not rejected in V'.
2. Termination: Every request will eventually be committed to the log by a majority of nodes.
3. Agreement: A value v is committed in a view V if and only if it was proposed in V and was not rejected in any previous view.
Proof outline:
- Assume that there exists a value v that has been committed in view V.
- By definition of the Commit phase, v was proposed in view V' and was not rejected in any previous view.
- Since there are more than 2/3 honest nodes, at least one honest node must have received a majority of Prepare messages for v in view V'.
- This honest node will then commit v to its log and send a Commit message to other nodes.
- By the definition of the Commit phase, v will be committed to the log of a majority of nodes.
Therefore, the modified PBFT algorithm with the modified View Change Protocol ensures safety in the presence of up to 1/3 Byzantine nodes.
